title: Funding to Cover Payroll
seo_title: Funding to Cover Payroll: Bridge the Gap | Fidelity Funding
meta_description: Payroll due and cash short? Learn why gaps happen, what you owe employees and how funding to cover payroll can bridge a short-term shortfall responsibly.
dek: Missing payroll damages trust and carries legal risk. Find the cause of the shortfall first, then decide whether short-term funding fits.
intro: It is Wednesday, payroll runs Friday, and the money you expected from a customer has not landed. You can see the shortfall in your account and you know exactly who depends on that check. Few moments in business feel more urgent, because employees cannot wait the way a vendor sometimes can.

Funding can bridge a one-time timing gap, but the better question is why the gap exists. This page covers common root causes, the legal side of paying wages and payroll taxes, the options owners use to bridge a shortfall and how to avoid turning a temporary problem into a recurring one.

paragraphs: A payroll shortfall usually comes from one of a handful of problems. Receivables are slow because customers pay in forty-five days while employees are paid weekly. A seasonal dip arrived before you built a reserve. A large expense, such as an equipment repair, ate the cash. Or margins are too thin to support current staffing.

The first three are timing problems that funding can bridge. The last is a structural problem that funding will only postpone. Look at your last six months of statements and ask whether the shortfall is a dip or a trend.

Write down the exact date and amount of the shortfall and the date money is expected in. A gap of four days is a different problem than a gap of four months, and the answer to 'how much do I need and for how long' determines nearly every choice that follows. Many owners ask for more than the shortfall because they are anxious, then pay for the extra on every payment. Precision saves money.

Employers must generally pay wages on time under state law, and payroll taxes withheld from employees are held in trust for the government. Late wages can bring penalties, claims and, in some states, personal liability for owners. Payroll tax issues carry especially serious consequences.

Rules vary by state and situation, so confirm details with an employment attorney, your payroll provider or a CPA. If you are about to miss a deposit, talk to a professional before choosing a workaround.

Keep a short written record of what you told employees and when payments were made. If a deposit or a paycheck must slip, honest early communication is almost always better received than a missed deposit with no explanation. Your payroll provider can also explain which deadlines are fixed and which have a grace period.

sections.h2: Options to bridge a short gap
paragraphs: Several tools can cover a few weeks. You can request faster payment or a deposit from customers, factor invoices, use a business line of credit if you already have one, take working capital through a funding partner or, in some cases, personally contribute funds. Each has costs and tradeoffs.

Compare total payback rather than the headline amount. A small advance of $20,000 at a factor rate around 1.2 would mean $24,000 repaid, an example only. If the shortfall is a few days, a smaller, shorter-term option usually costs less than a large one you will not need.

sections.h2: Fixing the cycle so it does not repeat
paragraphs: After the immediate crisis, build a thirteen-week cash flow forecast that lists expected receipts and obligations by week. It shows the next gap before it arrives, giving you time to act rather than react.

Shorten payment terms, ask for deposits, invoice immediately and follow up on late accounts. Aim to keep a reserve equal to some portion of a payroll cycle. Even a modest buffer turns an emergency into a routine adjustment.

A practical habit is a weekly ten-minute review every Monday: list what is due this week and next, what is expected in, and the projected balance each day. When the projected balance dips below zero, you have days or weeks, not hours, to respond. That is the cheapest form of funding there is, because it lets you negotiate from calm.

sections.h2: Warning signs that funding is the wrong tool
paragraphs: If you are covering payroll every month with new advances, the debt is likely compounding the problem. Stacking multiple advances can create heavy daily or weekly payments that consume the revenue you need to run the business.

If that sounds familiar, consider whether consolidating or restructuring existing obligations, cutting costs or revisiting pricing would help more than adding another payment. A funding specialist or accountant can help you weigh the choices honestly.

Fidelity Funding is a broker that connects you with funding partners, not a direct lender. The application is short and the first review uses a soft credit pull, so your score is not affected. A funding specialist reviews options with you, decisions can often come within hours and funding can sometimes arrive within about a day once approved. Terms vary by partner and underwriting, and nothing is guaranteed.

Tell the specialist how long the gap will last and when the money is due back to you. That lets them aim for the smallest, shortest solution that works. If payroll is close, start the application today.

key_takeaways: Find out whether the shortfall is a timing dip or a structural trend.
Wage and payroll tax rules carry real legal risk; confirm with a professional.
Choose the smallest and shortest bridge that works.
Use a rolling cash forecast to prevent a repeat.

faq.q: Can I get business funding to make payroll?
faq.a: Often yes, through working capital arranged with funding partners. Approval, amount and cost vary by partner and underwriting and are not guaranteed. A specialist will review your revenue and bank activity to see what options may fit the gap. Share the amount and timing of the gap so the review can focus on the right size and length.

faq.q: What happens if I cannot make payroll on time?
faq.a: Consequences depend on your state and circumstances but may include penalties, employee claims and damage to morale. Payroll taxes carry serious penalties. Contact an employment attorney or CPA promptly, and communicate with your team rather than staying silent. A short call with your payroll provider can clarify deadlines and options.

faq.q: Is invoice factoring better than a cash advance for payroll?
faq.a: If your problem is slow-paying customers with solid invoices, factoring may line up well because funding is tied to receivables. If there are no invoices to sell, other working capital may fit better. The right choice depends on your situation and total cost. Speak with a specialist to compare the costs side by side before you choose.

faq.q: How can I avoid payroll shortfalls in the future?
faq.a: Build a thirteen-week cash forecast, shorten customer payment terms, collect deposits and hold a small reserve. Review the forecast weekly. Seeing the gap a month ahead gives you time to negotiate, cut costs or arrange funding on better terms. Review it every week with your bookkeeper.
